title: Perez versus Wooden Joe, and trumpet mutes
summary: He compares Perez's leading with Wooden Joe's hardness and variation, then describes coconut-shell and plunger mutes.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Yeah. What about Woodsville?
How would he compare with Baraz? You say he had a big tone, loud.
Yeah, he had a big tone, loud, loud.
Did he always play cornet or did he? Did you think he switched the trumpet in his last day?
Well, in the later days he switched the trumpet. But when I first met him, he was playing one of those cornet, E-flat cornet.
E-flat?
Mm-hmm. The little tiny one? Yeah.
What about Wooden Hill? How would he compare with Barrage?

Well, I mean, Wooden Hill was a strong trumpet player. But for leading the band, Perez was one of the best. I mean, he used to lead them marches and all. I mean, in other words, he was a musician and all. In other words. But for hardness, for outlasting, I think Wooden Hill was one of the hardest trumpet players they had around Yard.
And what about variations? But Wooden Hill just played straight lead?
No, he'd vary. He'd vary.
He could get off and everything.
Yeah. He'd vary. But he was a hard man.
Did Perez use mute much?
Mute?
Yeah.
Well, yeah, occasionally in the dance hall, like they used to play at the roof garden. Well, I mean, they had the session. The session would use mutes together.
Oh, that's it. Now, what about Wooden Hill? What kind of mutes would he use?
Well, I tell you, Wooden Hill was so strong. Half of the time when he had a mute, now you didn't know he had it. That's the way he got that dance from Wooden Hill.
Well, I know they used to make mutes out of so many different things. I was wondering what different kind of mutes you'd seen.

Well, he had coconut shell. They used to take a coconut and cut it in half and gut out the meat. And they had another little straight mute they used to put in there. Before, wow-wow mutes came in style. They used to wow-wow with that, you know. Put the little mute in there and wow-wow with the half of coconut. Wow-wow, wow-wow, wow-wow, wow-wow.
Is that like a con mute that they had in there?
Yeah.
A pear-shaped?

That's right. Like a little light bulb? Yes. Like a little light bulb. Looked like a little light bulb. Yeah. Then eventually after that they started taking Chris Keller came behind. Well, I mean, he started taking those rubber plungers. And he started making them out of that. Later in the years, I mean, came wow-wow mutes and all the way. You didn't have to use all that. What you had to do is put your hand on it and work it.
